response.expected_mechanical_delta: Before (at the cutoff commit, pinned scope): archguard:detect_cycles reports one 6-member SCC {root, cli, fan-in, gate, gate/config, gate/factories}, and a position-based count of real import/export statements matching './cli' among the root-layer files = exactly 2 (serve-sessions.ts, serve.ts). After: the same position-based count = 0; the enumerated SCC member set at the pinned scope no longer contains cli; cli's inbound-edge count from the former members = 0; and the total number of nodes participating in cycles strictly decreases. Pre-registered prediction: 6 -> 4 ({root, gate, gate/config, gate/factories}), because fan-in's only return path threads root->cli — a measured 5 would falsify that reachability claim rather than the cut. Additionally each relocated symbol has exactly one definition site repo-wide, and scripts/test.sh stays green. Caveat on measurement: the before-reading must be taken at the cutoff commit — the working tree has since moved past it (HEAD already reads `import { runDriver } from "./driver-control.ts"` and `from "./driver-vocab.ts"`), so a before-reading taken now would be vacuous.
response.negative_control: Four controls, all of which must be run, because all four failure forms are indistinguishable from success on a file-diff reading. (1) Duplication control — the cheapest way to make the two edges vanish is to copy the primitives into root and leave cli's copies: assert that each relocated symbol is declared in exactly one file repo-wide and that cli imports rather than redeclares it; a green cycle metric plus two definitions is a regression, not a fix. (2) Re-export-shim control — an cli/ barrel that re-exports the moved modules keeps a root->cli value edge alive if root imports through it: verify on the IMPORTER files (serve.ts, serve-sessions.ts) that the specifier does not traverse cli/, not merely that the moved files no longer mention cli. (3) Mutation control — reintroduce exactly one root->cli value import and confirm detect_cycles puts cli back in the SCC; if the reading does not flip, the instrument is not measuring the edge you think it is. (4) Relocation control — assert the third quantity (total nodes in cycles) strictly decreases, not merely that cli left; a primitive moved into a module that already reaches root swaps membership and cuts nothing. Plus a not-evaluated guard: detect_cycles must return evaluated:true with an enumerated member list at the pinned scope — a bare empty list, or an unpinned-scope call, is the graph failing to be read, not the graph being clean.
response.abandon_or_reconsider_condition: Abandon or materially revise if any of the following is measured. (a) The pre-change control shows root->cli is not exactly 2 static value edges — a type-only or dynamic edge, or a disagreement between the position-based grep and the archguard reading, invalidates the enumeration and therefore the derived property; go back to investigation. (b) No cycle-free home exists: every candidate home for a primitive is itself reachable from root, so the change relocates the cycle instead of cutting it and the total cycle-node count does not fall — the edge is then load-bearing at the layer level and the concern must be re-framed (cut a different SCC edge, or declare the direction and accept the cycle). (c) Measurement shows one of the two 'shared primitives' is in fact used only by cli, with the core consumer's use being the accident — the ownership reading is falsified for that edge and the consumer-side cut (slice 2) is the right answer for it. (d) The post-change member count does not strictly decrease. (e) An independent reading of history shows the cli/ placement was deliberate rather than an accident of first consumption.

A fourth form is a reading rather than a change: a detect_cycles result that is empty because the scope was not pinned — the graph failing to be read, reported in the same shape as the graph being clean.

response.minimum_sufficiency_rationale: The derived property is binary and joint: cli leaves the SCC only when BOTH inbound edges from within the cycle are gone, and the findings establish the edge set is closed at exactly 2 (the other 34 run the normal way, and every other SCC member contributes zero edges into cli). Slice 1 removes exactly that set and nothing more — no smaller slice can work (one edge removed leaves one inbound edge and the cycle persists, so the dead-symbol cleanup is a free rider rather than a fix), and anything larger edits edges the findings show are not the problem, or chases the residual gate sub-cycle that the cut itself proves is not this concern's. It requires no new package, no new layer and no new instrument: the guard against regression is the ratchet and the layer declaration that already exist. And it fixes the cause named by the ownership reading rather than its symptom — the primitives are shared, so the answer is that core-root owns them and cli consumes them, not that cli should keep a facade core reaches back into.
